pins.name: c5
pins.note: The period-5 successor cycle on the glyph-calculus carrier. Named `c5` because that is the name the corpus's own rows use -- `PROVE period(c5) = 5` -- and a registry whose keys do not match the names rows reference is a registry nothing can look anything up in. The name is the lookup key for `presentation_ref` and for the `period(NAME)` decider, so renaming it is a wire-visible change, not cosmetic. This is the system the Symbol Game corpus's own claims are about -- 'PROVE period(c5) = 5' and 'LAND successor^2(alpha) = gamma' are statements about exactly these five rules. Two properties worth stating because they are the reason it is a useful pin rather than a decorative one. It is NOT terminating: successor cycles forever, so no length argument applies and is_length_reducing is false. Its reachable set from any carrier symbol is nevertheless the whole carrier, which closes, so the host can decide joinability over it -- which is the closure-not-termination doctrine this module rests on, exercised on a real system. And every rule has a single-symbol left-hand side, so no two rules overlap and the presentation has no critical pairs at all; by the critical pair lemma it is therefore locally confluent, and NOT_JOINABLE can never be emitted under it.

pins.name: c6
pins.note: A NEGATIVE CONTROL, and the only pin here that is not a system the corpus's own claims are about. It exists to falsify a specific wrong implementation, and that is stated rather than implied. Examiner's g(5) = 6: on five symbols the maximum order of a permutation is six, realised by a 2-cycle beside a 3-cycle. This is that permutation -- alpha <-> beta, and gamma -> delta -> epsilon -> gamma -- so its period is lcm(2, 3) = 6 while its signature has five members. Any checker that reports the SIZE of the signature returns 5 and is wrong, and c5 cannot detect that because for a single cycle the two numbers coincide. It is a real permutation system, so every verdict the host reaches about it is sound; pinning it vouches for nothing false. What it does NOT do is describe anything the Symbol Game corpus asserts, which is why the distinction from c5 is written here. A second pin also sharpens an existing fence: with two entries, the 'just use the only pinned presentation' shortcut for successor^k is no longer merely unsound in principle but ambiguous in fact.
